## 1. Size Anatomy of `viewer_2026-06-11k.html` (25,874,743 bytes; 25,387,052 chars)

| Component | Chars | % of file |
|---|---|---|
| `DATA.transcripts` (2,493 entries, keyed `{result_set}/{run_dir}`) | 15,706,414 | 61.9% |
| `DATA.subagent_transcripts` (500 run-keys) | 5,769,578 | 22.7% |
| `DATA.runs` (2,493 runs, criteria + tool_failures) | 3,537,630 | 13.9% |
| `DATA.result_sets` + `cases` + `model_pricing` (53 sets) | 83,303 | 0.3% |
| `PRECOMPUTED` JSON | 86,702 | 0.3% |
| HTML/CSS/JS shell (everything else) | 181,318 | 0.7% |

**What splitting saves:** transcripts + subagent_transcripts = **21.48 MB (84.6%)**. Initial payload after split = shell + PRECOMPUTED + DATA-minus-transcripts ≈ **3.9 MB** (~15% of current), gzipping well as JSON. `DATA.runs` (3.5 MB) must stay inline: every section's JS computes from it (`filteredRuns`, `buildPhaseAgg` ~L2198, `buildAgreeAgg` ~L2426, `caseMatrixHtml` ~L2579, Costs Detail `perfectByModel` ~L2845). Only `renderRunDetail` (template L3078, L3117) reads transcripts — a perfectly isolated seam.

**Shard distribution (transcripts + subagents combined, per result set):** 53 sets; max 1.17 MB (`20260609_004353`), mean 403 KB, median 275 KB, min ~11 KB. Per model: 17 models at 0.8–1.6 MB each. Per run: median 6.8 KB, p90 10 KB — 2,493 files is too many requests.

## 2. Proposed Multi-File Architecture

**Bundle layout** (inside the daaf-product site folder; relative paths only, since the deploy script rewrites them):

```
daaf-product/daafbench/           (or sibling daafbench/ dir, linked Learn > Choosing Your Model)
├── index.html                    # shell + inline DATA (sans transcripts) + PRECOMPUTED
└── data/
    ├── transcripts_manifest.json # {result_set: {file, n_main, n_subagent, bytes}}  (optional; can inline in DATA)
    └── tx_{result_set}.json      # {"transcripts":{...}, "subagent_transcripts":{...}} for that set, 53 files
```

**Shard strategy — recommend one file per `result_set`.** Rationale: (a) the lookup key is already `{result_set}/{run_dir}` (generator `load_transcripts` docstring L807-825; template L3078), so the shard name falls directly out of the key prefix — fetch `data/tx_{r.result_set}.json` and index by the same composite key; (b) 275 KB median / 1.17 MB max is a good on-demand fetch size; (c) sets are append-only archival units, so shards are naturally immutable across regenerations; (d) per-model sharding (17 × ~1.27 MB) cross-cuts the key scheme and means a user browsing one result set's runs touches many files. Per-run (2,493 files) is excessive; a single 21.5 MB file defeats the purpose. Bundle main + subagent transcripts for a set in one file (both are looked up together in `renderRunDetail`).

**JS changes (all confined to Run Explorer):**
- `renderRunDetail` becomes two-stage: render header/criteria/tool-failures synchronously (all from `r`), render a "Loading transcript…" placeholder, then `fetch()` the shard (memoized in a module-level cache, mirroring the anatomy page's `fetchDocument` memoization pattern — `daaf_anatomy.js` §§ DOCUMENT_FETCHING) and fill the transcript blocks in.
- Callers needing awareness: `selectRun` (L3465), `renderRunExplorer` (L2984), `jumpToRun` deep links (L3478) — deep links with `&run=` must await the shard before scrolling is "complete," or simply let the transcript pop in.
- Failure fallback: explicit message in the detail panel — "Transcript could not be loaded (this page must be served over http(s); see Provenance for the archived run directory)" — never a silent empty section.
- Add a tiny in-flight guard so rapid run-list clicking doesn't render a stale transcript into the wrong run (compare a request token against `state.selectedRunIdx`).

**Generator changes:**
- `--output` becomes a bundle directory; auto-increment moves to the dir name (`daafbench_2026-06-12a/`), preserving the no-overwrite versioning convention (resolve_paths L87-95).
- `generate_html` keeps `__DATA_JSON__` substitution but the bundle drops `transcripts`/`subagent_transcripts` keys from DATA, replacing them with a `transcripts_index` (set → relative path + counts) so the JS knows what exists without a manifest round-trip.
- Shard writer: per set, `json.dumps` with the same `_strip_nonprintable` hygiene; the `\u003c` escaping (escape_embedded_json L1638-1655) is only needed for the *inline* remnant — fetched JSON never passes through the HTML parser, but keeping the same serializer everywhere is harmless and simpler.
- **Keep a `--single-file` flag** emitting the current monolith. This is the file:// mitigation (below) and preserves the local-audit workflow at near-zero cost since data prep is shared.

**file:// implications:** `fetch()` of sibling files is blocked on `file://` origins in both Chrome and modern Firefox (CORS/unique-origin). Recommendation: **explicitly drop file:// support for the bundle** (transcripts unavailable; fallback message + a one-line `python3 -m http.server` hint), and keep `--single-file` for offline auditing. The template's existing `isFileProto` hash handling (L1431-1443) stays valid either way.

**README impact (§ 8 + § 12):** § 8's "self-contained HTML… works opened directly from disk" claim and the artifact description need rewrite; the "Viewer current" bullet's single-file naming convention (§ 12, `viewer_2026-06-11k.html` lineage) needs a bundle-naming successor; `benchmarks/.gitignore`'s `viewer_*.html` pattern needs a companion for bundle dirs. The **http(s) retest list grows from three to four**: explicit-nav hash writes, scrollspy `replaceState`, `content-visibility` anchor rendering (§ 8 design-record item 7), **plus transcript fetch-on-demand including the failure fallback and the `&run=` deep-link path**.

**Gap analysis / least-invasive path:** The viewer's dark slate + indigo is already *adjacent* to the site — `#0f172a` vs `#0a0f1c` surfaces, and the site's `--accent-indigo` **is** the viewer's `#6366f1` accent. The cohesion gap is mostly: (1) fonts (biggest visual delta), (2) the teal-led accent hierarchy and 3px gradient strip, (3) the topbar/footer chrome, (4) radii/spacing generosity. **Recommendation: token swap + fonts + topbar/footer, not a full restyle.** The viewer's CSS already routes nearly all color through `:root` custom properties (template L26-42, "WP8 sweep"), so remapping `--surface-0/1`, `--border-1`, `--text-1/2/3` to site values and adding `--accent-teal` is structurally cheap. One deliberate caution: site teal `#22d3a8` sits close to the status-pass green `#34d399`; keep the audited status ramp untouched and use teal for chrome/links/active states only (or keep indigo as the in-content interactive accent) so "accent" never reads as "pass."

## 4. Risks & Sequencing

**Fragile under restyling:**
1. **Hardcoded hex in JS-generated SVG** — `svgCostFrontier` gridlines `#1e293b`, axis text `#94a3b8`, frontier `rgba(52,211,153,.8)` (template L3260-3299); legend swatches mix `var(--accent-light)` and literals (L2143-2146); `MODEL_COLORS`/`MODEL_COLORS_LIGHT` (L1025-1028). A surface-token swap without a JS hex sweep leaves invisible gridlines/mismatched charts.
2. **Inline styles in render functions** — `renderRunDetail`, `caseMatrixHtml`, transcript blocks carry literal `#cbd5e1`, `#fcd34d`, `#1e293b`, `#475569` etc.; the noscript block (L477) too.
3. **Contrast audit invalidation** — `.rs-3`/`.rs-na` alphas were tuned against `#0f172a` (WP8 audit, L233-240); changing surfaces requires re-measuring the 4.5:1/3:1 floors.
4. **Scrollspy + anchors vs an 88px sticky topbar** — `updateActiveLink` uses a hardcoded 120px offset (L3411), `scroll-padding-top:18px` (L46), TOC rail `top:0` (L59). All three must become nav-height-aware or the topbar breaks active-state detection and hash jumps land under the bar.
5. **`content-visibility` intrinsic sizes** — `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 900px/2600px` (L93-100) were calibrated to current type metrics; DM Sans at 1.7 line-height changes section heights — re-verify hash deep-links and scrollbar behavior (already on the http(s) retest list).
6. **Print/noscript**: no print stylesheet exists (deferred fast-follow, README § 12 L1182-1188) — no regression, but worth re-confirming the deferral.

**Sequencing — architecture split FIRST, styling second.** (1) The split is surgically bounded (generator output stage + `renderRunDetail` seam) while styling touches the entire shell plus a JS hex sweep; doing styling first means re-verifying it all again after the split. (2) Post-split, the shell is a ~180 KB reviewable artifact and regeneration is decoupled from 21 MB of data — making styling iteration materially faster. (3) The contrast re-audit, scrollspy offset rework, and `content-visibility` re-check should each happen exactly once, against the final topbar geometry. Within styling: tokens + fonts → topbar/footer chrome → component idioms (badges/callouts/cards) → JS hex sweep + WP8 re-audit.

## Gaps and Limitations
- daaf-product `get-started.html`/`learn-understanding.html` and open-augments `workshops.html` were not read beyond token extraction; nav/footer were verified identical on two pages, assumed consistent on the rest.
- The anatomy JS was skimmed structurally only (per instructions); its markdown renderer/fetch memoization were identified by name, not read line-by-line.
- Gzip transfer-size estimates are not computed (deploy compression is outside the container).
- The deploy script's exact relative-link rewriting rules are unknown; the recommendation assumes plain relative `data/…` fetch URLs survive it — worth confirming with the user.
